polix_malaysia_fiscal.scope: Federal petroleum revenue, taxation, subsidies, GLC governance, federal-state fiscal relations

actors.name: PETRONAS
actors.formal_mandate: National petroleum corporation. Sole concessionaire for upstream oil/gas under Petroleum Development Act 1974.
actors.resource_access: Full upstream petroleum rights. Downstream, gas, LNG, shipping, solar, hydrogen.
actors.decision_authority: Board-appointed. PM as Minister of Finance (Incorporated) is sole shareholder.
actors.accountability_paths: Annual report to Parliament. Auditor-General review. But operational autonomy is high.
actors.notes: Structural dual role: commercial entity AND national resource custodian. Dividend policy is politically sensitive.

actors.name: Ministry of Finance (MoF)
actors.formal_mandate: Federal fiscal policy, budget, taxation, government investment.
actors.resource_access: Federal budget, taxation powers, PETRONAS dividends, debt issuance.
actors.decision_authority: Budget allocation, tax policy, subsidy design, fiscal transfers.
actors.accountability_paths: Parliament, Cabinet, PM (who is also MoF).
actors.notes: PM holds MoF portfolio — concentration of fiscal + executive power.

actors.name: Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM)
actors.formal_mandate: Monetary policy, financial stability, currency management, Islamic finance regulation.
actors.resource_access: Foreign reserves, monetary policy tools, regulatory authority.
actors.decision_authority: OPR (interest rate), FX intervention, bank licensing, macroprudential policy.
actors.accountability_paths: Board of directors. Annual report to Parliament. Governor appointed by PM.
actors.notes: Relatively independent. Governor appointment is political but operational independence is maintained.

actors.name: Securities Commission (SC)
actors.formal_mandate: Capital market regulation, investor protection, market integrity.
actors.resource_access: Regulatory authority over Bursa Malaysia, fund managers, listed companies.
actors.notes: Regulatory capture risk from industry revolving door.

actors.name: State Governments (esp. Sabah, Sarawak, Terengganu)
actors.formal_mandate: State-level governance, land, natural resources (state jurisdiction under Constitution).
actors.resource_access: Petroleum royalty (5% standard, 10% claimed by East Malaysia), state land, timber, minerals.
actors.decision_authority: State-level resource policy, land allocation, state GLCs.
actors.accountability_paths: State legislature. Federal fiscal transfers create dependency.
actors.notes: East Malaysia has stronger resource claims under Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63). Federal fiscal transfers create leverage.

actors.name: Cabinet / Economic Planning Unit (EPU)
actors.formal_mandate: National development planning, public investment, GLC oversight.
actors.resource_access: Development budget, GLC appointments, mega-project approval.
actors.decision_authority: 5-year plans, GLC board appointments, project greenlighting.
actors.accountability_paths: PM and Cabinet. Parliament for budget approval.
actors.notes: EPU has outsized influence on allocation without proportional public scrutiny.

rent_flows.beneficiary: Federal government (via PETRONAS dividend + petroleum tax + export duty)
rent_flows.cost_bearer: State governments (fixed 5% royalty, not profit share), future generations (depletion), local communities (environmental)
rent_flows.estimated_annual_value: RM 60-80B (PETRONAS dividend + tax + royalty, varies with oil price)
rent_flows.reversibility: STRUCTURAL — requires legislative change (Petroleum Development Act 1974)
rent_flows.notes: The 5% royalty cap is a structural rule asymmetry. States with petroleum bear extraction costs but receive a fixed fraction.

rent_flows.reversibility: MEDIUM — requires regulatory reform, political will
rent_flows.notes: Approved Permits (APs) and licensing create artificial scarcity. Classic regulatory capture.

rent_flows.beneficiary: Consumers (diffuse), but disproportionate benefit to high-consumption households
rent_flows.cost_bearer: Federal budget (RM 50-80B annually), future fiscal space
rent_flows.reversibility: HIGH — politically sensitive, successive governments struggle
rent_flows.notes: Subsidies are regressive in practice (rich consume more fuel). B40-targeted replacement is technically feasible but politically costly.

rent_flows.cost_bearer: GLC performance, minority shareholders, public trust
rent_flows.reversibility: MEDIUM — requires governance reform, appointment independence
rent_flows.notes: GLC board appointments are political patronage instruments. Performance impact is real but hard to isolate.

rule_asymmetries.description: Petroleum royalty capped at 5% for states. Federal receives majority of petroleum revenue.
rule_asymmetries.notes: Constitutional + legislative. Sabah/Sarawak claim 10%+ under MA63. Political negotiation ongoing.

rule_asymmetries.description: PM holds MoF portfolio. Executive and fiscal authority concentrated in one person.
rule_asymmetries.who_benefits: PM/executive branch (fiscal discretion without Cabinet constraint)
rule_asymmetries.notes: Convention, not law. But structural concentration of power is documented.

rule_asymmetries.description: GST replaced by SST — regressive shift reducing tax base and fiscal resilience.
rule_asymmetries.who_bears_cost: Federal fiscal space (RM 20-25B annual revenue loss), future generations
rule_asymmetries.notes: GST is economically superior (broader base, self-enforcing chain). SST is politically easier but fiscally weaker.

coercion_signals: Federal fiscal transfers create state dependency
PETRONAS dividend pressure during low oil prices
Subsidy reform political cost exceeds fiscal benefit in short term
geopolitical_exposure: US rate cycle (MYR pressure, capital flows)
polix_malaysia_fiscal.notes: Seed case. Public sources only. No insider knowledge. Requires cross-validation with BNM, MoF, PETRONAS primary data.

polix_petronas_glc.scope: National petroleum corporation and government-linked investment companies

actors.name: PETRONAS Board
actors.formal_mandate: Strategic oversight of national petroleum corporation.
actors.resource_access: Full upstream/downstream petroleum, LNG, solar, hydrogen.
actors.decision_authority: Capital allocation, dividend recommendation, strategic direction.
actors.notes: Board appointments are political. But operational competence has historically been high.

actors.name: Khazanah Nasional
actors.formal_mandate: Sovereign wealth fund. Strategic investments. GLC restructuring.
actors.resource_access: RM 100B+ portfolio. Major stakes in CIMB, Axiata, PLUS, IHH, etc.
actors.decision_authority: Investment decisions, GLC board appointments, fund allocation.
actors.notes: Dual mandate: commercial returns AND strategic national interest. Tension is structural.

actors.name: PNB (Permodalan Nasional Berhad)
actors.formal_mandate: National unit trust. Bumiputera wealth accumulation.
actors.resource_access: RM 300B+ AUM. Major stakes in Sime Darby, Maybank, UMW.
actors.notes: Largest fund manager in Malaysia. Social mandate (Bumiputera equity) is explicit.

rule_asymmetries.description: GLC board appointments are political patronage instruments, not merit-based governance.
rule_asymmetries.who_bears_cost: GLC performance, minority shareholders, public trust
rule_asymmetries.notes: Malaysia Corporate Governance Code exists but enforcement is weak.

civx_malaysia_2027_2040.scope: Federal fiscal sustainability under oil price × demographic × reform scenarios

assumption_axes.name: oil_price_brent
assumption_axes.description: Brent crude average price path over horizon

assumption_axes.name: demographic_path
assumption_axes.basis: DOSM population projections, UN World Population Prospects

assumption_axes.name: fiscal_reform
assumption_axes.description: Whether GST/broader tax base is reintroduced

paths.name: Managed transition — high oil + fiscal reform + demographic adaptation
key_risks: Oil price reversal after investment lock-in
paths.option_space: Full fiscal flexibility. Investment capacity for energy transition. Social safety net funded.
paths.notes: Best case requires political will that has historically been absent. Not impossible but not baseline.

paths.name: Muddle through — base oil + partial reform + demographic drift
key_risks: Fiscal deficit widens as petroleum revenue declines
MYR depreciation pressure from twin deficits
paths.option_space: Limited fiscal flexibility. Incremental reform possible but structural change deferred.
irreversibility: Lost decade of energy transition investment
paths.notes: Most likely path based on historical pattern. Not optimal but survivable.

paths.name: Structural decline — low oil + no reform + rapid aging
key_risks: MYR crisis (capital flight, FX reserve depletion)
Social unrest from subsidy removal pressure
Pension/healthcare funding gap for aging population
paths.option_space: Very limited. IMF-style conditionality possible. Sovereignty compromised.
irreversibility: Human capital loss (10+ years to replace)
paths.notes: Low probability but high consequence. Requires combination of adverse factors. Worth studying, not worth panicking.

calibration_data: Historical fiscal deficit vs oil price correlation (2000-2025)
PETRONAS actual dividend vs budget assumption accuracy
GST revenue vs SST revenue actual comparison
DOSM population projection vs actual (2015-2025 validation)
limitations: Not calibrated against historical fiscal outcomes
Political economy variables are deep uncertainty
External shocks (pandemic, war, financial crisis) not modeled
No Monte Carlo — discrete paths only
Resilience scores are ordinal, not cardinal
civx_malaysia_2027_2040.notes: First CIVX seed. Three paths, five assumption axes. All interpretations tagged. Sovereign decision required before any path is promoted to decision-eligible.
